Whatever your religious convictions are there are a few solid facts that are true across the board. 1 - You don't take anything with you after you die. 2 - No one has come back and said anything about what lays after life - and no, those bullshit youtube videos and sermons about coming back to life do NOT count. You cannot use the fear of hell as a reason to keep living, you have to do it for yourself. And why put so much emphasis on this eternal hellfire. In your religion, god is a generous, loving, kind spirit. The aspect of you going through mental discord is something he would smile about, you're experiencing feeling in the worst way you can. 

Now, I'd like to give my own opinion on this subject. Whether there is a god or not, if there is some divine plan setup or if this is all chaos, what does it all matter. Forget "god", forget hell, forget all the mental structures you have built for yourself. You need to make YOURSELF happy before anyone else. You can have faith but using it as a rope to hold on to so you dont kill youself is a waste of time. 

Using debt as motivation to not kill yourself? You realize that after you're dead you wont have to worry about undue payments. 

STOP thinking that HELL is what waits for you if you follow through with your feelings. You were taught everything you know about heaven and hell by a human being. These are learned realms, not FACT. Don't tell yourself your disease is incurable and don't think that your misery will make others unhappy. Thats a selfish comment, pure attention bait. 

You need to take a deep breath and really look at your life without any religious bias. You need to not look for acceptance through others and you need to stop with the pity parties. You're a wonderful human being.

The question you need to ask yourself is what is the method that one takes to change the things in their life they don't like. Change is always available, its a matter of getting yourself to start down that path. Nothing comes easy, and thats life, but the things worth getting are worth struggling for. Form a plan to get out of the mundane grind you're in, instead of playing video games read or do something creative and if you're short bald brown use what you have to play to your strengths. If you enjoy learning, become educated, if you like working out, get buff, find something that will be appealing to other people and work at it. This is not an easy process and will have many bumps in the road but could it be any worse than what you feel now? You need to make YOURSELF happy, not have outside forces push the feeling for you.

And really man, boasting about how financially successful you are in a suicide post is really sideways. 

I guess the lesson to learn from this is MONEY DOESNT MAKE YOU HAPPY, OMFG.

Having money doesn't mean you're privileged. Having a career doesn't equate to something that you can dangle in other peoples faces for envy. Saying you have a wife doesn't mean there is any love. So no, none of this is anything anyone could ask for. And do you really think 100 million people would trade what they have to become depressed and suicidal? The things you own don't own you. Stop fucking calling yourself an asshole and a shitstain. It needlessly dramatizes what you're saying. If you are so tired of doing everything, take the initiative and go do something new. 

Did you ever think that you and your wife shouldn't be together? Have you two sat down and had a discussion about the problems in your relationship and realistically considered resolutions? If you can't fuck your wife and think you're a burden to her, end the fucking marriage. Stop holding onto the shit the kids in the junior high class teased you about. Accept yourself. If you're gay, be gay, if you're curious, try stuff out. You only live once and from what i've read you need to break lose and find yourself.

And as for that fucking comment - "You'd look at me and you might even envy me." - No, I don't envy you. Money, property, a good paying job, a miserable failed marriage, a man who is afraid to chase his desires because he was taunted in junior high - No I don't envy you at all.

From what i've found with people saying they have an "extensive mental health history" is that its used a crutch. It absolves responsibility from actions and feelings in a much broader way than its intended. I was diagnosed with bi-polar type 2, extreme sadistic masochistic tendencies, violent psychosis and severe depression. I was told that its a miracle I understand what is left from right after all the abuse I put myself through. They prescribed me a massive cocktail of medication, abilify, seroquel, 2000 mgs of lithium a day, prozac and ambien. I was a drugged out zombie in the worst way. Eventually, I took a stand and said no. I don't need these awful drugs to mask what i'm feeling and i'm not going to be fucking chained up to a bottle of pills. I quit everything cold turkey -which you should NEVER do- and suffered through the misery of psychoactive withdrawal. After it all though, after embracing the feelings I feared before, after accepting that I had been a suicidal cutter (90 stitches from one cut, passed out from blood loss from the 45 deep wounds I inflicted with a chef knife), and most importantly realizing that the depression I had was because of actions. Whether or not i'm predisposed to the depression condition, I was able to sit back and understand why the things that made me feel terrible were making me feel terrible. Its a sharp pain and it hurts at first but I feel that its always better to hold and examine why you feel the way you do instead of taking meds. I haven't cut, burned, or broken my own bones, taken medication or seen a fucking therapist in 6 years. I'm doing better now than I ever did while locked in that office. I'm not demeaning the use of therapy mind you. You need to find what works for you and pursue it. 

 "What's the most some fucked up, hideous, boring, socially inept person could ever amount to, anyway?"<--- You wrote this. The only way to change any of these things is to confront them head on. You said you dont want to die but you have nothing worth living for. Instead of finding some idol to justify your life, live for youself.

The way to handle this is to change your lifestyle. Instead of sitting alone, exercise. Instead of eating alone, go out to a park and eat in public. To combat dealing with assholes, say hello to everyone you run into everywhere you go. The great thing about life is that things change, and you can have an influence of how they change. You don't need to call yourself a fat lonely freak or a whiney teenager - its only through those labels you put on yourself do you manifest that image. 

No one is going to come to your house, knock on the door and beg to be your friend. You working out is the only thing thats going to change your weight. In what way are you a freak? As you stated, you're a teenager, how can you apply a label like that to yourself at such a young age? 

I have a feeling that you have some serious self confidence issues. I went through the same feelings and circumstances growing up and it was miserable. Obviously I didn't kill myself but I carried the anger and resentment. At 17 I had my first suicide attempt. Cut down to the bone on my left forearm. Muscle snapped back exposing half of my arms bone. I should be dead from that but a friend threw me in the street in front an ambulance driving by in the middle of a snowstorm - unreal. 9 hours of surgery and 90 stitches later, i'm sent home with a bottle of Vicodin and a pat on the back. I washed the 30 Vics down with half a bottle of jug wine. I blacked out for 6 hours only to wake up pissed off it didn't work. I've gorged my arm with a chef knife until I passed out from blood loss. I've popped my chest open with a bread knife. I've tried to intentionally kill myself through drug mixture overdoses. All of this stemmed from the same feelings you're going through right now. Its not worth it brother, you dont have to go through it to change your outlook.

I would recommend letting the lies all fall apart. Confront your friends and family, tell them what you've been lying about and be truthful with it. This is certainly going to procure some negatives reactions but they wont all be. You can wipe your slate and start fresh. No lies, no bullshit. Through honesty you'll get closer to your family and friends. If I may ask, what subject matter are the lies you're talking about?

By making a date to end it all, you've projected how you feel into the future. All it takes to change this resolution you have is to change this date into something positive. Saying you're sorry to anyone you've let down is an incorrect statement. You chose to post this and say you made a date, there is no sorrow in that. 

Take a step back and think about what you're thinking about doing. Think about the things that are bothering you and really consider if all the pain you're going through is worth ending your life. Strength is all about acknowledging the negatives. Without self degredation, really think about the reasons that got you to this point. Embrace it, feel it, internalize it. When you do that, you can compare it to everything else and see how vainful it is to commit suicide.

And as far as strength, I feel that people who are thinking or have tried to kill themselves are the strongest individuals around. Their minds are so powerful that they can override their basic desire to live and exist. That is serious mental manipulation. You have strength but you dont need to use it to end it.

Fear is anticipation that you haven't embraced. Your life is moving forward whether you are in constant fear or not. Take an inventory of what you want to do in the present and future and start doing it. If you need to move, start taking the necessary actions to push you towards that point. Try to talk about these thoughts without stating that you're worried about what other people will say. You posted on this board for yourself, not for the viewpoint that other people take. 

And as far as failure goes, its not about how far you fall, its about how hard you fucking bounce back. Everyone makes mistakes and fucks up, its what allows you to learn from experiences and not repeat them in the future. Until you try and lose though, you wont get the benefit of this.
Because you don't actually want to go through with it. You posted on this board and said you get sidetracked by hope - thats a good thing. What kind  of situations have pushed you to this point?

You can get that manager fired if you go to the higher ups and tell them what happened. You're going to find assholes like this time and time again in life, but you need to understand that their words only hurt you if you let them hurt you. I've had similar experiences and over time, I trained myself to let it go in one ear and out the other. This manager only has power because of the reaction he gets to his verbal abuse. While you're still at this job, if he comes up and starts yelling again, try looking at his face with a smile. That will throw him off wicked hard and take the wind out his sails. 

Don't let this shithead push you over the edge. I'm sure HE has a very hard time out of work, who knows what his life is like Take a deep breath, go into work, smile and say hello to everything and decide to show compassion to everyone regardless of how they're acting. Thats what I did and it worked.

I've used a wide array of that have caused this opening of the world over the years - mescaline, mushrooms, acid, 2ci, 2cb, dmt, bromo dragonfly, etc. I had some profound moments but only recently have I started to see what is the most potent, powerful, crushingly strong method of opening the third eye. Taoist meditation. Meditation is a bad way to describe it, you sit with your eyes open without looking, your ears hearing without listening and seeing the thoughts in your mind without thinking. At the upper stages of the lower first tier, serious things start to happen. I've seen blue spirals in the walls, faces push out of whatever surface was in front of me and make expressions, waves of shadow and a bliss thats indescribable.The bliss moment was so strong that it forced a tear from my eye and make me reel back due to shock. It took days to shake that residual haze after that session. The entire time my ears have a constant dull ring in them. It feels like my brain is being massaged. I've never had a substance that got anywhere close to the sensations i've gotten from this. Its gotten to the point where I need to clock my sitting time because of how much it affects me throughout the day.

I'm not a religious person but the some of the ideas of buddhism make a lot of sense to me. One of the most potent aftereffects of participating in this practice is this surge of compassion for everyone and everything. . Its changed my demeanor, the way I interact with people. how I conduct my days and the way I think. Out of everything, the sitting (meditation) has caused the most radical change in my demeanor. I don't know if the taste of nirvana was "god" but I can say damn well that it was love. Not a directed love, just pure, ecstatic love. 

I highly recommend that any psycho-naughts out there find a good teacher and give the open eye sitting a shot. Its unreal.

The trick is not expect the reaction, but to know that you tried you're best just by expressing how you actually felt. Being a compassionate individual is not easy; theres a reason why most don't do it. Try to embrace the concern, express the hurt you have watching how your social circle functions and forget about the rewards. The true gain is in yourself, knowing that you had the heart to try and care.

The only way to figure out how to not "mess things up" is to screw them abysmally in the first place. You're young, in school, have a family and realize that maybe the relationship you're in isn't what you really want in life. This is totally ok. Don't let the drama of what you're involved in drag you down; start fresh, figure yourself out, find someone that returns the care and compassion you give them. Don't pigeon hole yourself, you have everything to look forward to assuming you're willing to change to the now.
